meta_description: Peak-ready fulfillment platform — throughput up 26% through peak and infrastructure cost per order down 21%

blocks.x: Peak-ready fulfillment platform, throughput up 26% through peak and infrastructure cost per order down 21%
Identity withheld, a fulfillment group whose year was four weeks long and whose platform met those four weeks on hope and autoscaling bills. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline post-mortem priced the hope: peak-day throughput capped by order-orchestration hot paths, infrastructure spend tripling for a quarter, and one cascade failure that took two sites offline for six hours at the worst moment.
Capacity planning ran on last year's peak plus 20%. This year's peak arrived plus 60%, and the platform discovered its real limits in production.

We rebuilt for the peak as an engineering standard: order orchestration decomposed with backpressure at every boundary, load models built from real order shapes and rehearsed in game days before peak, multi-site failover tested with actual traffic shadowing, and the cost ledger per order reported continuously so scale decisions trade money, not mystery. Peak became a rehearsal, not an exam.
